name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Stephen Lynch seeking re-election with large financial advantage
Republican opponent raised only about $1,500 with negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 97%
model.rationale: Lynch holds a heavily Democratic Boston-area seat, has out-raised his opponent by hundreds of thousands of dollars, and faces a Republican campaign with essentially no funding. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win, so the forecast stays near the baseline with no evidence warranting a shift.
model.watch: Any late outside spending surge or unexpected polling showing a competitive race would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Stephen Lynch, a longtime Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win another term in this Boston-area district, which leans Democratic by about fifteen points. He has raised over $900,000 and holds more than $640,000 on hand, while Republican Robert Burke has raised roughly $1,500 and reports negative cash on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly against Lynch, but nothing suggests a serious challenge.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, the district's partisan lean, and the lopsided financial picture. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit margin. A minor-party candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources.
